original_test_intent: Validate the BMC Operations Firmware inventory and perform one approved compatible BMC or server-component firmware update through the supported workflow, proving correct activation and health.
original_method: Correlate all BMC/server inventory entries with exact hardware and active/staged state, select one owner-approved component and target version, validate signed image compatibility and update/activation dependencies, preserve configuration and recovery access, upload/activate once with final approval and stable power, monitor the task and any reboot, then prove the expected active version, configuration and platform health with rollback only under the vendor plan.
manual_activity: The owner selects the exact component/image/version and gives final activation approval; an operator verifies stable power and recovery, observes the reboot/task boundary and owns rollback and verdict decisions.
safety_requirements: Never flash an ambiguous component or image
Verify signature/checksum and hardware compatibility before upload
Use validated TLS and protected secret injection
Maintain stable power and independent recovery
Update one component only per approved transaction
Obtain final approval immediately before activation
Do not automatically retry a failed or stalled task
Stop on wrong target, health alarm, access loss or unexpected component change
Preserve update/SEL/OS logs and do not clear evidence
agent_execution_scope: Validate image identity, signature and compatibility
Upload/activate one approved component after confirmation
Monitor task, activation and reboot with bounded polling
Assist only approved rollback and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve maintenance, activation and recovery plan
Control rollback/vendor escalation and decide PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: FirmwareInventory GET is useful baseline evidence only; it cannot upload or activate firmware, identify active versus staged version, verify image compatibility or provide rollback, and `-k`/command-line credentials are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-supported BMC Web/UpdateService path for one signed, mapped and approved component image, monitor the bounded task/activation/reboot and verify the active post-version plus health and configuration.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC/server information, one firmware update, new-version check and 15/15-minute estimates remain; component/image/version are required owner inputs rather than inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: SINGLE-COMPONENT SIGNED FIRMWARE UPDATE WITH ACTIVE-VERSION PROOF
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Maintain an update ledger linking hardware inventory URI, active/staged baseline, image hash/signature, compatibility approval, task ID/events, activation/reboot, post active version, configuration/health delta and any rollback.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target and image assurance, task semantics, recovery and active-state verification while preserving the source update.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only inventory covers only the first inspection step; reachability after upload does not prove correct component activation or absence of unrelated changes.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A valid image for the wrong board revision can brick the component; firmware may also report a staged version until a separately scoped reset or power cycle occurs.

project_override_considerations: The Project must choose the single component this general row updates and define whether any required activation reset belongs inside this case. The following OEM Firmware row covers a multi-device OEM matrix and must not share a generic one-component result.
expected_evidence: Verified target/component/active-staged inventory, target version, release/compatibility and maintenance approval
Signed image provenance, checksum/signature, backup and independent recovery proof
Protected upload/task/activation responses and bounded progress/reboot timeline
Complete post-update inventory proving intended active version and same component identity
Configuration and BMC/server health comparison, update/audit/SEL/OS logs and no unrelated changes
Approved rollback/recovery evidence if needed and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requires BMC/server inventory, a firmware update and new-version verification. The exact component is unspecified but is a normal owner selection, not a competing source target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The component, signed image, compatibility, activation and recovery package are normal vendor/project prerequisites; the update lifecycle is identifiable without guessing them.

review_improvement: Restores the omitted firmware write and converts a generic inventory read into a one-component, signed, recoverable update whose active version and side effects are auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: A firmware version string is meaningful only when tied to exact hardware and activation state. UpdateService may expose multiple inventory entries and staged images, so a post-upload version alone can be misleading. The evidence chain must bind image-to-component before write and task-to-active slot after activation, while recovery exists independently of the component being updated.
